findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that constructs a genuine content conflict (not an untracked-overwrite) and asserts the merge aborts, keeps local, and emits the fsck-recover hint, pinning AC #2's unchanged-behavior guarantee.
evidence: Test steps 1-4 all exercise the untracked-overwrite abort/recovery; none construct a genuine content conflict.
AC: 'A genuine content conflict still aborts, keeps local, and hints rebar fsck-recover (unchanged behavior).'
findings.finding: The test plan enumerates the untracked-overwrite recovery path (RED/GREEN/mutation) but does not include an explicit test for the genuine-content-conflict fallback, which AC #2 promises remains unchanged (abort, keep local, hint fsck-recover).
scenarios: A refactor of the error-signature parser accidentally matches a content-conflict error and quarantines/retries instead of aborting, silently changing conflict behavior with no failing test.

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Force a stable locale for the git invocation and its parse (e.g. run git with `LC_ALL=C`/`GIT_...` or `-c core.quotepath=...`) so the untracked-overwrite signature and named-path list match deterministically regardless of the ambient locale; add an assertion or note that detection is locale-independent.
evidence: Plan quote: 'when git merge fails, detect the "untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge" signature and parse the exact paths git names'
git honors LC_MESSAGES/LANG and emits localized error text and translated path-list headers, so a hardcoded English substring/parser is locale-fragile
findings.finding: The fix detects the abort by matching git's English error string "untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge" and parses the paths git names, but git localizes this message per LC_MESSAGES. Under a non-English locale the substring never matches, so the self-heal never engages and the store re-wedges exactly as before the fix.
findings.location: Fix (primary) — 'detect the "untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge" signature and parse the exact paths git names'
scenarios: Developer workstation or CI runner (macOS/Linux/Windows) with LANG/LC_MESSAGES set to a non-English locale (e.g. de_DE, fr_FR): git prints the translated error, the English signature match fails, git merge --abort runs, and the user sees the identical store-wedge / stranded-local-commits loop the fix was meant to cure.
findings.suggested_fix: Invoke the merge with `env LC_ALL=C git merge ...` (or set it in the subprocess env) so both the signature string and the path-list block are always in the C locale, then parse against that fixed wording.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name a RETIRE/cleanup path for quarantine directories (e.g. `rebar fsck-recover` prunes them, or an age/count-based sweep), so the safety copies do not accumulate without bound.
evidence: Plan quote: 'Relocate ONLY those named untracked paths into a quarantine directory under the git common dir ... Quarantine is retained as a safety copy (not deleted inline).'
Each self-heal creates a new timestamped subdirectory; nothing enumerated ever removes them
findings.finding: The quarantine directory is explicitly 'retained as a safety copy (not deleted inline)' but the plan states no RETIRE/cleanup path, so quarantine copies under <git-common-dir>/reconverge-quarantine/<utc-ts>/ accumulate unboundedly across every self-healing reconverge.
findings.location: Fix (primary) — 'Quarantine is retained as a safety copy (not deleted inline).'
scenarios: A long-lived clone that reconverges repeatedly (e.g. a CI worker or a busy developer checkout) grows an ever-larger reconverge-quarantine tree inside the git common dir, leaking disk and cluttering the repo internals with no bounded lifecycle.
findings.suggested_fix: State that fsck-recover (or a bounded age-based retention) is responsible for pruning quarantine dirs, and note it in the fsck-recover hint path.

findings.checklist_item: [ ] State whether the untracked-overwrite collision can also wedge the push-retry path (`_recover_dirty_merge`, which matches the same `_DIRTY_WD` signature but only handles tracked files); either extend the quarantine+retry there or justify why that seam is out of scope.
evidence: push_classify.py:142-144: `_DIRTY_WD` matches 'would be overwritten by merge' — which is exactly the untracked-overwrite signature the plan parses
_recover_dirty_merge (push_recovery.py:118-189): `_stash_create` omits -u and `reset --hard -q` is tracked-only, so an untracked collision re-fails and returns False
Plan problem statement: 'push-recovery cannot clear untracked files (push_recovery.py: git reset --hard is tracked-only; _stash_create omits -u)'
findings.finding: The fix patches only `_union_merge` (reconverge), but the same origin-introduced untracked-overwrite also wedges the push-retry path: `push_recovery._merge_remote_under_lock` routes any message matching `_DIRTY_WD` ('would be overwritten by merge') to `_recover_dirty_merge`, whose stash (`_stash_create`, no -u) and `reset --hard` are tracked-only, so the untracked collision re-fails and returns False there too. The plan names this limitation in the problem statement but does not state why the push-retry seam is out of scope for the wedge.
scenarios: compaction leaves the tracker dirty and the next store MUTATION goes through push (non-fast-forward recovery) rather than a read-triggered reconverge — the untracked collision recurs at the push seam the fix does not touch

findings.checklist_item: [ ] Pin git's message locale (e.g. run the merge under LC_ALL=C) or otherwise make the untracked-path extraction locale-robust, and define the fallback when the path list cannot be parsed.
evidence: Existing module matchers (push_classify.py `_DIRTY_WD`, transport markers) already assume English stderr, so this is codebase-consistent, but extracting a structured PATH LIST from localized prose is materially more fragile than a substring signature match
No mention in the plan of pinning the git locale (e.g. LC_ALL=C) around the merge or of a fallback when the path list cannot be parsed
findings.finding: The plan parses the EXACT list of paths git names out of the merge stderr. Git's 'The following untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge' block is locale-sensitive (LANG/LC_MESSAGES), so both the signature match AND the path-list extraction can silently miss under a non-English git, degrading straight back to the abort-only wedge without signalling why.
findings.location: Fix (primary): 'detect the ... signature and parse the exact paths git names'
scenarios: reconverge runs in an environment where git emits localized diagnostics; the signature/path parse fails and the merge falls through to abort — the wedge is not broken and the failure looks identical to today
findings.suggested_fix: Invoke the collision-detecting merge with LC_ALL=C so the 'untracked working tree files would be overwritten' block and its indented path list are stable to parse; on any parse miss, fall through to the existing abort-and-hint path.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify quarantine-move failure handling: on any relocation error, do not retry — fall back to `git merge --abort` and leave the working tree unchanged (copy-then-verify or atomic-rename-with-fallback), and surface the error rather than swallowing it.
evidence: Plan quote: 'Relocate ONLY those named untracked paths into a quarantine directory under the git common dir ... then retry the merge once.'
A rename across a filesystem boundary (git common dir vs worktree on a different mount) fails EXDEV; the plan's only enumerated failure branch is 'any other failure ... git merge --abort'
findings.finding: The plan assumes the quarantine MOVE always succeeds before retrying the merge, but a move can itself fail (cross-device rename, permission, path collision inside quarantine); the recovery does not specify behavior when the relocation partially fails.
findings.location: Fix (primary) — 'Relocate ONLY those named untracked paths into a quarantine directory ... then retry the merge once.'
scenarios: A worktree and git-common-dir on different mounts (or read-only quarantine parent): the relocation fails or leaves paths half-moved, and the retry then aborts — but the plan does not state that a failed/partial move is safely rolled back or reported, risking a worktree left in an inconsistent state.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reuse push_classify._DIRTY_WD for the 'would be overwritten' signature match in _union_merge (import it) rather than adding a second regex, confining the NEW code in sync.py to the path-list parser that _DIRTY_WD does not provide.
evidence: push_classify.py:142-144 defines `_DIRTY_WD = re.compile(r"would be overwritten by merge|local changes.*would be overwritten", re.IGNORECASE)`
push_recovery.py:272 already uses `_DIRTY_WD.search(merge.stderr or "")` to route this exact abort class to recovery
The path-list PARSING (extracting the files git names) is genuinely new — no existing code does this — so only the signature-match half overlaps
findings.finding: The plan's new signature detector for 'untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge' partially duplicates the existing push_classify._DIRTY_WD regex, which already matches the 'would be overwritten by merge' string and is the established store-wide detector for this abort class.
findings.location: Fix (primary) — 'detect the "untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge" signature'; file_impact bullet for src/rebar/_store/sync.py ('add a small parser for the git error's path list')
scenarios: A second, subtly-different regex in sync.py drifts from _DIRTY_WD when git's wording changes, so the two detectors disagree on what counts as a dirty-worktree abort
findings.suggested_fix: In _union_merge, gate the quarantine branch on `push_classify._DIRTY_WD.search(merge.stderr or "")` and add only the path-extraction parser as new logic. If the untracked-specific wording must be distinguished from the tracked-'local changes' wording, tighten _DIRTY_WD or add one narrow sibling marker in push_classify next to it, keeping all overwrite-signature detection in one module.
